q: 1. The relation between modulus of rupture fcr, splitting strength fcs, and direct tensile strength fq is given by
explain: Among the different tensile strength measures of concrete, the flexural (modulus of rupture) value is the highest, followed by the split cylinder strength, with the direct tensile strength being the lowest: fcr > fcs > fct.

q: 2. The approximate value of the ratio between direct tensile strength and flexural strength is
explain: As given in this text, the direct tensile strength of concrete is approximately half (0.5 times) its flexural strength (modulus of rupture).

q: 3. The relation between modulus of rupture fcr and characteristic strength fck is given by
explain: As per IS 456, the flexural strength (modulus of rupture) of concrete is related to its characteristic compressive strength by fcr = 0.7√fck.

q: 4. The compressive strength of 100 mm cube as compared to 150 mm cube is always
explain: Due to the size effect in concrete testing, smaller 100 mm cube specimens generally record a higher apparent compressive strength than standard 150 mm cubes.

q: 5. The modulus of elasticity E of concrete can be taken as
explain: As per IS 456, the static modulus of elasticity of concrete is commonly estimated using the empirical formula E = 5700√fck (in N/mm²).

q: 6. The concrete mix which causes difficulty in obtaining a smooth finish, possess
explain: A harsh concrete mix, characterized by excessive hardness/lack of fines, makes it difficult to achieve a smooth surface finish.

q: 7. The top diameter, bottom diameter, and the height of slump mould are
explain: As per IS 1199, the standard slump cone mould has a top diameter of 10 cm, bottom diameter of 20 cm, and a height of 30 cm.

q: 8. If the slump of concrete mix is 60 mm, its workability is
explain: A slump value of 60 mm falls within the medium workability range according to the standard slump classification table.

q: 9. The grade of concrete not recommended by IS 456 is
explain: As per the classification referenced in this text, M30 does not appear among the listed standard grades recommended by IS 456.

q: 10. The grade of concrete M150 means that compressive strength of a 15 cm cube after 28 days is
explain: In the older grade-naming convention (M followed by a number in kg/cm²), M150 directly denotes a 28-day cube compressive strength of 150 kg/cm².

q: 11. According to IS 456, the number of grades of concrete mix is
explain: As per the classification referenced in this text (older IS 456 provisions), concrete mixes are designated into seven standard grades.

q: 12. The preliminary test is repeated if the difference of compressive strength of three test specimen exceeds
explain: As per the acceptance criteria in this text, the preliminary test must be repeated if the difference in compressive strength among the three test specimens exceeds 15 kg/cm².

q: 13. The main purpose of concrete design mix is
options: mixing the concrete in better way
explain: Design mixing proportions the ingredients scientifically to achieve the required strength and durability at the most economical cement content, making cost economy its main purpose.

q: 14. For the construction of RCC slabs, columns, beams, walls etc, the grade of concrete mix used is
explain: For general RCC structural elements like slabs, columns, beams and walls, the nominal mix commonly used is 1:2:4 (equivalent to M15 grade).

q: 15. Generally nominal mix is done by volume while design mix is done by
explain: Design mixes require accurate proportioning of ingredients, which is achieved by batching materials by weight rather than the less precise volume batching used in nominal mixes.

q: 16. For the construction of the retaining structures, the type of concrete mix to be used is
explain: For retaining structures, a richer mix of proportion 1:1.5:3 (equivalent to M20 grade) is recommended for adequate strength and durability.

q: 17. If the average compressive strength is 4000 kg/cm2 and standard deviation is 500, the coefficient of variation is
explain: Coefficient of variation = (standard deviation / mean) x 100 = (500/4000) x 100 = 12.5%.

q: 18. Ordinary concrete is not used for concrete grade
explain: Ordinary (nominal mix) concrete is only applicable to lower/moderate grades; higher grades like M40 require designed/controlled mix proportions and cannot use nominal mix ratios.

q: 19. The following proportion of the ingredients of concrete mix is not in conformation to arbitory method of proportioning
explain: The arbitrary method of proportioning follows a consistent pattern where the coarse aggregate proportion is twice the fine aggregate (as in 1:1:2, 1:2:4, 1:3:6); the ratio 1:4:10 breaks this pattern, so it does not conform.

q: 20. If X, Y, Z are the fineness modulus of coarse, fine and combined aggregates, the percentage p of fine aggregates combined aggregate is
explain: As per the standard fineness-modulus blending formula used in this text, the percentage of fine aggregate in the combined aggregate is given by P = (X−Z)/(Z−Y) × 100, where X, Y, Z are the FM of coarse, fine, and combined aggregate respectively.

q: 21. Gel space ratio is defined as the ratio of
options: volume of hydrated cement to the sum of volume of hydrated cement and capillary pores
the sum of volume of hydrated cement and capillary pores to volume of hydrated cement
both a) and b) of above
explain: Gel-space ratio is defined by Powers as the volume of the gel (hydration products) divided by the sum of the volume of the gel and the capillary pore space it occupies.

q: 22. The minimum grade of concrete for pre-tensioned member is
explain: Pre-tensioned members require high early strength to allow release of the tendons, so a minimum grade of M40 concrete is specified.

q: 23. For batching 1:3:6 concrete mix by volume, the ingredients required per bag of 50 kg cement are
options: 70 litres of sand and 120 litres of aggregates
70 kg of sand and 140 litres of aggregates
105 litres of sand and 140 litres of aggregates
105 litres of sand and 210 litres of aggregates
explain: For a 1:3:6 mix, with one bag of cement corresponding to about 35 litres, the sand requirement (3×35=105 litres) and coarse aggregate requirement (6×35=210 litres) work out to 105 litres of sand and 210 litres of aggregate.

q: 24. The dimensions of 35 litres forma for measuring aggregates by volume are
options: length 30 cm, breadth 25 cm, height 30 cm
length 39 cm, breadth 25 cm, height 32 cm
length 27 cm, breadth 27 cm, height 48 cm
length 22 cm, breadth 25 cm, height 40 cm
explain: As per the standard farma box dimensions given in this text, a box measuring 22 cm × 25 cm × 40 cm gives a volume corresponding to 35 litres.

q: 25. Light weight concrete is used in
explain: Because of its lower strength and density, light weight concrete finds its principal application in non-load-bearing wall construction such as partition walls.

q: 26. For reinforced concrete exposed to sulphate attack minimum grade required is
explain: As per the durability requirement referenced in this text, the minimum grade specified for reinforced concrete exposed to sulphate attack is M10.

q: 27. The ferrocement is a composite material obtained by
options: random disposal of short, discontinuous fibres in the conventional concrete
reinforcing the cement mortar with steel fibres in the form of wire mesh
blending ferrous compounds in the ordinary Portland cement
explain: Ferrocement is defined as cement mortar reinforced with closely spaced layers of continuous, relatively thin steel wire mesh, distinguishing it from randomly dispersed fibre-reinforced concrete.

q: 28. The volume of reinforcement in ferrocement (percent) normally varies between
explain: In typical ferrocement construction, the volume fraction of the wire mesh reinforcement generally lies in the range of 5% to 8% of the total volume.

q: 29. For mass concrete in piers and abutments, the concrete mix used is of proportion.
explain: For mass concrete work such as piers and abutments, a leaner mix of proportion 1:3:6 is generally used, as high strength is not the primary requirement.

q: 30. For highly loaded columns, the concrete mix used is of proportion .........:
explain: Highly loaded columns require a rich, high-strength concrete mix, so a proportion of 1:1:2 (equivalent to a high grade) is used.

q: 31. The correct proportioning of various ingredients of concrete largely depend upon.............
explain: Correct mix proportioning must account for bulking of sand, water content, and aggregate absorption together — all of these factors affect the actual quantities batched.

q: 32. For high degree of workability, the slump value should vary between
explain: As per the slump classification used in this text, a high degree of workability corresponds to a slump value in the range of 80 to 100 mm.

q: 33. The concrete in which preliminary tests are preformed for designing the mix is called:
explain: Controlled concrete refers to concrete whose mix proportions are determined and controlled through preliminary laboratory tests to meet specified strength and durability requirements.

q: 34. The individual variation between test strength of sample should not be more than
explain: As per test acceptance criteria, the deviation of an individual test result from the average of the sample should not exceed ±15% of the average value.

q: 35. Age factor for permissible compressive stress in concrete after six months is :
explain: Concrete continues to gain strength with age, so codes allow an age factor of 1.20 to be applied to the permissible compressive stress for concrete that is six months old.
